requirements.text: The key words MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT, and MAY are to be interpreted as described in RFC 2119 and RFC 8174.
Clients MUST validate the event id and Schnorr signature according to [NIP-01](01.md) before processing any event defined here.
A parser used for this NIP MUST reject duplicate top-level JSON member names. All public keys, event ids, change hashes, and SHA-256 values defined here MUST be 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters.
`created_at`, relay arrival order, subscription order, relay URL, and transport path MUST NOT determine document state, control order, authorization, checkpoint selection, or conflict resolution.
The acquisition channel MUST NOT change validation or document state. A client that republishes a carrier MUST preserve the complete signed event.

Every required tag defined here MUST appear exactly once and MUST contain exactly the elements shown in its event definition. A required tag is invalid when it is missing, repeated, missing a value, contains extra elements, or has a malformed value.

Tag order does not affect protocol meaning. Unknown tags MUST be ignored and MUST NOT change v1 state. An extension that changes identity, authorization, dependencies, or state requires a new protocol version or event kind.

Durable events of kinds `1624`, `1625`, `1626`, `1627`, and `31624` MUST NOT contain a [NIP-40](40.md) `expiration` tag or the [NIP-70](70.md) protected-event `-` tag. Other authorized devices may need to preserve and republish the same signed history.
The `content` of manifests, controls, checkpoint descriptors, and checkpoint chunks MUST use the JSON Canonicalization Scheme defined by [RFC 8785](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8785).
A v1 decoder MUST reject:
Arrays declared as sorted MUST already be sorted. Consumers MUST NOT repair signed content before validation.
Binary content MUST use standard RFC 4648 base64 with padding. URL-safe, unpadded, whitespace-tolerant, and non-canonical forms are invalid.
A conforming v1 client MUST accept valid objects up to these limits:
Clients SHOULD share public documents using a [NIP-19](19.md) `naddr` for the manifest, with relay hints where useful.
Each editing installation MUST use a distinct device key.
A removed device key MUST NOT appear in a later control. Reinstatement, device replacement, or privilege elevation uses a fresh device key and therefore a fresh ActorId.
A device key SHOULD NOT be active on more than one installation. If a key is cloned, the equivocation rules below protect convergence but cannot restore confidentiality or trust.
Before invoking an Automerge parser, a client MUST validate this framing:
A valid change MUST decode and encode to the same bytes:
Equivalent APIs may be used. The result MUST match the language-neutral v1 test vectors.

The v1 Automerge profile uses 32-byte actors, UTF-16 code-unit text indexing, time 0, no message, empty extra bytes, the listed v1 action/object/scalar/column/mark semantics, and treats unknown semantics in a declared v1 object as invalid.

For candidate C and its exact accepted dependency closure D(C), next_op(C) MUST be 1 when D(C) contains no operations and otherwise 1 plus the greatest operation counter visible in D(C); C.start_op MUST equal next_op(C), and all arithmetic and conversions MUST be checked for overflow.

Actor sequence MUST start at 1 and increment exactly for that actor; for seq greater than 1 the exact accepted dependency closure MUST contain exactly one same-actor change with seq - 1, while an empty change consumes sequence without advancing the causal operation counter.
A control frontier contains at most 64 heads. When a document has more heads, an authorized writer SHOULD create empty Automerge merge changes before the control is issued.
A merge change may contain at most 256 dependencies. Producers SHOULD sort heads by decoded ChangeHash bytes and build a bounded fan-in chain until the final frontier contains at most 64 heads.

The manifest fields and limits defined by the draft MUST be enforced. Its selected control reference MUST resolve against stateful outcomes for the same coordinate: an accepted control is an available canonical hint, a statefully valid excluded control is an available noncanonical hint, a missing or pending control is pending/unavailable, and any wrong-kind, wrong-coordinate, unsupported, statically invalid, or dynamically invalid control is invalid/unavailable; checkpoint and control references remain advisory and grant no authority.

The latest manifest MUST be selected according to NIP-01 before validating only that selected event; if it is pending, invalid, unsupported, or otherwise unavailable, clients MUST NOT fall back to an older manifest, and no manifest may select control history, grant authorization, or establish checkpoint trust.

- `seq` starts at `0` and increases by one; - genesis has no parent and an empty `base_heads` array; - `format`, `text_encoding`, and `policy` are fixed for the document; - members are sorted by decoded device pubkey bytes and contain no duplicate device key; - `account` is `null` or one Nostr public key and is fixed from the device's first appearance; - roles are sorted, unique, non-empty, and contain only `checkpoint` and `write`; - `write` authorizes change events; - `checkpoint` authorizes checkpoint descriptors and chunks; - the controller has no implicit device role; - an existing device's later role set MUST be a subset of its earlier role set; - a removed device key MUST NOT reappear; - `base_heads` is sorted by decoded hash bytes, unique, an antichain, and contains at most 64 hashes; - every base head is accepted under the parent control; - for every writer retained from the parent control, the base closure contains that ActorId's highest accepted change in the parent accepted state; - `predecessor` is `null` except on genesis; - `successor` is `null` unless the control is terminal; and - a control is terminal when no member has `write`. A terminal control has no valid child.
A newly received lower-id sibling may change the canonical chain. Clients MUST retain signed evidence and rebuild derived state when this happens.
A producer MUST durably persist the exact signed control before signing a change or checkpoint that references it.
A producer SHOULD publish the control before publishing dependent carriers. A client that receives a dependent carrier before its control MUST retain the carrier as pending.

After a dependent carrier has been signed, additional control durability MUST be obtained by republishing the same signed control event. The controller MUST NOT create a semantically equivalent control with a different event id and treat it as the same authorization epoch.
Clients SHOULD retain at least one complete valid carrier for every accepted ChangeHash.
Clients SHOULD preserve equivocation evidence and prompt the controller to revoke the device.
Clients MUST rerun this process from genesis when new evidence can change a control choice, dependency, or equivocation result.
Implementations may optimize storage and traversal. They MUST produce the same canonical controls, accepted ChangeHashes, excluded ChangeHashes, heads, and materialized document.

Final manifest, checkpoint-descriptor, and checkpoint-chunk event outcomes MUST be derived from complete dynamic selection, authorization, binding, completeness, and verification results rather than static ingress validity; verified checkpoints remain advisory and MUST NOT authorize or redefine history.
Checkpoint publication is optional. A conforming client MUST support ordinary change replay when no checkpoint is available.
The snapshot MUST be one complete Automerge `save()` made after closing pending transactions. Incremental saves and bundles are invalid.
`heads` MUST be sorted, unique, and equal the heads obtained after loading the snapshot.
The loaded change set MUST equal exactly the ancestor closure of `heads`. Extra disconnected changes make the checkpoint invalid.
`raw_size` MUST be greater than zero. `chunk_size` MUST be between `1` and `32768`. `chunk_count` MUST equal `ceil(raw_size / chunk_size)` and MUST be between `1` and `4096`.
The declared heads and all embedded changes MUST be accepted no later than the referenced control. A checkpoint MUST NOT include state authorized only by a later control.
All declared counts and limits MUST match the loaded snapshot.
The index, count, chunk size, chunk hash, proof, and descriptor root MUST validate.
All non-final chunks MUST have the descriptor `chunk_size`. The final chunk contains the remaining bytes.
After assembly, the client MUST verify:

Every change embedded in a usable v1 checkpoint MUST have at least one valid carrier and the client MUST verify the full control chain, signatures, actors, counters, dependencies, frontiers, and equivocation rules.
Checkpoint parsing SHOULD use bounded memory and deterministic work budgets. Local budget exhaustion is not proof that a checkpoint is invalid.

Clients SHOULD open a live subscription before, or together with, historical backfill. All received events are deduplicated by Nostr event id. Document changes are additionally deduplicated by ChangeHash.
Clients SHOULD use [NIP-77](77.md) when available. NIP-77 reconciles event ids; actual carriers still move through ordinary `EVENT` and `REQ` messages and are validated by this NIP.

A plain `EOSE` marks the stored/live boundary. It does not prove that a relay returned every matching stored event. Clients SHOULD use [NIP-67](67.md) hints when available and otherwise continue bounded pagination and dependency recovery.
A client MUST NOT claim global finality.

Producers SHOULD coalesce high-frequency local edits into bounded Automerge changes. They SHOULD publish at meaningful durability or interaction boundaries rather than publishing one event for every keystroke, pointer movement, or transient UI action.
A local commit MUST NOT wait for relay publication. Clients SHOULD durably persist signed carriers in a local outbox before network publication.

Retries are idempotent by event id. Clients SHOULD publish durable carriers to more than one independently operated relay and SHOULD read back important controls and checkpoint objects by exact event id.
Given the same complete set of relevant signed events, two conforming v1 clients MUST derive the same:
A suitable relay SHOULD:

Clients MUST NOT treat a relay's [NIP-11](11.md) declaration as proof of complete history, permanent retention, checkpoint availability, or CRDT validation. Relays implementing [NIP-77](77.md) advertise that capability separately.
Relays MAY require [NIP-42](42.md), payment, proof of work, or other local admission policy. Relay admission does not change document validity.

Relays are not required to retain complete document history indefinitely. Producers SHOULD use local durable storage and more than one retention domain. They SHOULD create a successor document before a document approaches the v1 resource limits or when its retention, privacy, membership, or governance boundary must be reset.
Application rules MUST NOT change the core control chain, accepted ChangeHashes, or Automerge heads defined by this NIP.
Large binary objects SHOULD be stored outside the Automerge document. The document may contain hashes and metadata for those objects.
A client MAY retain an unknown protocol revision or unknown Automerge profile as `unsupported_revision` evidence but MUST NOT apply it. Known-v1 unknown semantics are invalid.
Controller keys SHOULD be kept separate from routine editing keys and SHOULD have a tested recovery procedure.

Clients MUST enforce the v1 limits before large allocations where possible. They SHOULD use bounded workers for Automerge and checkpoint parsing and MUST avoid recursion or work that is unbounded by validated input limits.

A client claiming v1 conformance MUST pass language-neutral vectors for manifests, controls, changes, causal transitions, forks, equivocation, verified-history checkpoints, dependencies, and randomized delivery.
Each required vector MUST produce expected canonical controls, protocol dispositions, accepted ChangeHashes, heads, history_digest, dispositions_digest, typed state assertions, and alerts.

The vectors are maintained outside the NIPs repository and MUST be linked from the proposal before it is marked ready for acceptance. If the prose and a vector disagree, the prose in this NIP controls.
Implementations MUST treat kinds, limits, encodings, actor derivation, and selection rules as one sealed revision; applications cannot customize them while claiming conformance.

Canonical dispositions are accepted, pending, excluded, invalid, and unsupported_revision; every dynamically evaluated manifest, checkpoint descriptor, and checkpoint chunk MUST have exactly one canonical event-namespace disposition record included in the dispositions digest.
Complete, budget_exhausted, and cancelled are local completion states and MUST NOT alter canonical dispositions or disposition digests.
Recovery from a snapshot whose historical carriers are unavailable is outside v1 and MUST NOT be inferred from a manifest pointer.
The initial conformance contract MUST NOT define a digest over Automerge save bytes until independent byte-identical behavior is proven.
Clients MUST surface controller equivocation and canonical-control reorganization as integrity alerts.
Clients MUST surface the first device-equivocated actor sequence and affected changes as an integrity alert.
Draft protocol limits are sealed for the draft revision but remain production-provisional until measured cross-platform qualification.
The generic implementation MUST be a standalone snake_case repository/package/crate and MUST NOT depend on radroots_* crates.
The initial core MUST be deterministic, batch-oriented, network-free, database-free, async-runtime-free, FFI-free, and application-schema-free.
All Automerge calls MUST be isolated in the anti-corruption adapter.
Every protocol document construction/load MUST explicitly select UTF-16, disable migration, and reject partial load.
The canonical re-encoding path MUST be qualified as bounded, uncompressed, fallible, and cross-language compatible before it is used as a validity rule.
Public ingestion MUST begin from raw event JSON bytes so duplicate members can be rejected.
Invalid evidence for a ChangeHash MUST NOT poison a valid carrier for that ChangeHash.
The initial reference evaluator MUST perform deterministic complete batch reconstruction and serve as the oracle for optimized implementations.
Cargo features MUST NOT change protocol validity or conformance semantics.
The TypeScript implementation MUST be independently written and MUST NOT import or call the Rust implementation.

Document state and final change disposition MUST be keyed by ChangeHash across every carrier attributable to the evaluated coordinate. One dynamically valid carrier is sufficient. Invalid, pending, unsupported, or noncanonical carrier claims MUST NOT poison a hash accepted through a valid claim, and a hash already present in the selected accepted base MUST NOT be re-admitted as a new epoch candidate.

Every validated change carrier attributable to the evaluated coordinate MUST produce a represented ChangeHash outcome. A missing or pending referenced control produces pending; a wrong-kind, wrong-coordinate, statically invalid, dynamically invalid, or unauthorized referenced control produces invalid; and an otherwise-valid claim on a statefully valid noncanonical control produces excluded.

A current-epoch candidate that depends on a known earlier-epoch change outside the referenced control's accepted base closure is invalid. Only a dependency whose required evidence is genuinely absent or unresolved may keep the candidate pending.

Evaluation for one document coordinate MUST derive canonical controls, change and event dispositions, digests, checkpoint results, evidence output, and local work accounting only from evidence attributable to that coordinate, except that explicitly referenced predecessor or successor lifecycle evidence MAY be read as non-reportable support. Adding unrelated-document evidence MUST NOT change the target report or completion.

Every traversal, allocation, canonical-vector construction, and digest encoding whose cost depends on retained evidence, including interruption-report finalization after budget exhaustion or cancellation, MUST be covered by a deterministic work budget reservation or a sealed constant bound. No unreserved evidence-proportional work may begin after local execution has stopped.

Before full manifest validation, a validly signed kind-31624 event is attributable to a document coordinate for replacement selection when all syntactically valid d-tag document-id values collapse to exactly one distinct value and at least one such value exists. The event then participates in NIP-01 replacement ordering, but full validation still rejects missing, repeated, malformed, or extra-element d tags and no older manifest is used. An event with zero or multiple distinct valid document-id values is invalid and unattributable.

The canonical signed conformance distribution MUST include adversarial cases for change-before-control, pending and invalid referenced controls, cross-control duplicate carriers, accepted-base duplicate carriers, invalid-claim non-poisoning, pruned earlier-epoch dependencies, unrelated-coordinate isolation, malformed manifest replacement attribution, and exact interruption-report work boundaries.

Public final assurance MUST bind detailed test, coverage, mutation, resource, package, supply-chain, and interoperability artifacts to the exact final Rust implementation commit, opaque private TypeScript implementation commit, dependency locks, authority hashes, and signed fixture distribution. Older artifacts MUST be machine-marked as superseded.

The independent private TypeScript implementation MUST implement NCRDT-DUP-002, NCRDT-DISPOSITION-002, NCRDT-EPOCH-001, NCRDT-SCOPE-002, NCRDT-RESOURCE-002, NCRDT-MANIFEST-003, and NCRDT-CONF-005 without calling the Rust implementation, and MUST produce byte-identical canonical reports for the expanded signed distribution.
After final accepted and canonical-ancestor-pruned rules, any genuinely unresolved claim MUST yield pending before otherwise-valid noncanonical or conclusive-failure claims.
Implementations MUST retain reasoned per-claim and final-lineage state; a generic prior disposition MUST NOT replace the canonical ChangeHash reduction table.
A dependency known through another control, unusable control evidence, or prior equivocation-excluded history MUST be invalid for the selected signed epoch.
Only genuinely absent or unresolved selected-control dependency evidence MUST remain pending and MAY promote after delivery.

Checkpoint control resolution MUST distinguish canonical authorization, pending or missing evidence, noncanonical controls, and every known unusable control; only missing or pending control evidence yields a pending checkpoint.
One-coordinate evaluation MUST derive canonical output and local work only from attributable target evidence and explicit lifecycle support.
Every evidence-proportional operation after interruption MUST be conservatively reserved before canonical work and mechanically consumed.
When finalization capacity cannot be reserved, a client MAY return a constant-size interrupted report with no fabricated canonical progress.

The externally authored NIP MUST eventually contain every interoperability-critical rule required to reproduce language-neutral conformance without companion-only prose; this remains an explicit external reconciliation hold.
The mandatory signed corpus MUST cover mixed claims, complete dependency knowledge, checkpoint control states, coordinate resource isolation, and finalization boundaries.
A draft-v1 change that references unsupported control evidence MUST be invalid and MUST NOT inherit unsupported_revision.
Device, ActorId, and write-role authorization MUST be evaluated before canonical versus noncanonical branch disposition; an unauthorized noncanonical claim is invalid.
A change referencing a terminal control is invalid because no write authorization exists.
A child control with missing or pending parent evidence is pending; a child naming known wrong-kind, wrong-coordinate, static-invalid, dynamic-invalid, or unsupported parent evidence is invalid.
Pending parent state propagates pending to descendants, invalid parent state propagates invalid, and noncanonical descendants are excluded only after branch-relative transition validation.
A child base head accepted under the parent is usable; genuinely absent or unresolved heads are pending; known invalid, excluded, unsupported, or other-control heads make the child invalid.
A chunk with missing or pending descriptor evidence is pending; wrong-kind, wrong-coordinate, invalid, unsupported, or dynamically unusable descriptor evidence makes the draft-v1 chunk invalid.
Cancellation and capacity checks MUST precede target-proportional allocation; coordinate views MUST use retained indexes without cloning target evidence sets.
Every control, ChangeHash, carrier claim, reference lookup, and authorization comparison used to construct prior dependency knowledge MUST be deterministically metered and cancellable.

Every reserved finalization dimension MUST be mechanically consumed or explicitly refunded; unexplained remainder, underflow, overrun, cross-dimension borrowing, or double finish is an invariant failure.
Evidence-proportional report invariant validation MUST execute under reserved or separately charged capacity before finalization capacity is released.
The mandatory signed distribution MUST include the combined claim, parent, frontier, descriptor, chunk, terminal, and exact resource scenarios identified by remediation v6.
Every in-core normative requirement MUST bind an exact executed signed fixture or exact named assertion; broad repository tests or profile-only overlays cannot close consensus-critical behavior.
